slides.title: GaN Building Block Rev B
slides.subtitle:
Four EPC2361 per switch on one board, three legs on a PCB busbar:
a decision-driven design for a 1200 V, 300 kW Stacked Polyphase Bridge inverter
slides.author: Enes Ayaz · KTH Royal Institute of Technology · October 2026

slides.title: Design flow

rows: 1200 V, 300 kW, M ≤ 1.15, PMSM cos φ = 0.9 → 228 A_{rms} per leg
100–650 V Si/SiC/GaN survey → 100 V GaN, EPC2361
V_{m} + L·di/dt ≤ 90 V, even integer N → 75 V, N = 16
first-cut loop + LTspice → ≤ 80 A per device
loss, T_{j}, V_{DS} vs n → 4 EPC2361 per switch
loss vs MLCC count → ≥ 50 kHz; bypass 6 × 1 µF per cell + bank
one driver per pair (star, Kelvin) → building block of two cells
two blocks side by side, DC link and AC joined in copper → Rev B leg board
two isolated supplies + Zener bias, UFCS shunt per cell, U.FL, HO 250-S
legs share the 75 V bus → laminated PCB busbar under the legs
Q3D of leg + busbar, KiCad schematic = PCB, Rev B fab files

slides.title: Design inputs

rows: V_{DS} ≤ 90 V at nominal bus (100 V part)

paras: SPB: N three-phase submodules in series on the DC side, each feeding one winding set; V_{m} = 1200 V / N.

slides.title: Phase current follows from the inputs

paras: Each of the 3N legs delivers P/3N at V_{ph} = M·V_{m}/(2√2):
I_{rms} = P / (3 · M·V_{bus}/(2√2) · cos φ)
N·V_{m} = V_{bus}: the phase current does !!not!! depend on N
**228 A_{rms} per leg**, 322 A peak (cos φ = 0.9)
DC current per leg 83 A; series DC chain 250 A

items.text: Losses below are for cos φ = 0.9; the PMSM operating point must be confirmed with the machine design.

slides.title: Voltage class: why 100 V GaN

paras: At fixed bus voltage and phase current the minimum semiconductor loss scales with R_{DS(on)}·C_{oss,tr}
100 V GaN gives the lowest product among 100–650 V Si/SiC/GaN candidates
Selected: **EPC2361**, 100 V, 0.75 mΩ typ, 3 × 5 mm, top-side cooling

slides.title: EPC2361 key data

paras: Low threshold and −4 V limit: gate drive needs care (bump, negative bias)
Top of the package at !!source potential!!: the thermal interface must insulate
Seven interleaved stripes; pad 2 next to the gate is the natural Kelvin point (own net KH/KL on Rev B)

slides.title: Submodule voltage from L·di/dt

paras: Peak stress v̂_{DS} = V_{m} + L_{loop}·di/dt ≤ 90 V (10 % below the rating)
First-cut loop with MLCCs: ≈ 0.5 nH per cell
Fast switching (≈ 30 A/ns, analytical gate-charge model) ⇒ 15 V overshoot ⇒ V_{m} ≤ 75 V
N integer and even (symmetric submodules and winding sets): 14 → 86 V, 18 → 67 V and 12.5 % more parts

slides.title: Why not lower: every submodule costs parts and loss

paras: Phase current is fixed by P, V_{bus}, M, cos φ, not by N
Each submodule carries the full phase current ⇒ conduction loss, transistors, drivers and supplies scale with N
60 V (N = 20): +25 % parts and conduction loss
Overshoot margin rechecked with the final layout (Q3D, 0.374 nH per cell on Rev A; Rev B in step 11)

slides.title: First-cut power loop of one cell

paras: Loop = PCB copper (vertical loop over 0.1 mm dielectric, vias, pads) + ESL of the local MLCCs
Copper alone ≈ 0.31 nH; MLCCs in parallel add ESL/n_{c}
1 / 2 / 4 / 6 MLCCs: 0.79 / 0.55 / 0.43 / 0.39 nH: beyond ≈ 4 the number hardly matters
Part: 1 µF 100 V X7S 0805 next to the drains

items.text: Design with L_{loop} = 0.5 nH per cell (0.3 and 0.8 nH as bounds)

slides.title: One EPC2361 per switch: how fast and how much overshoot

paras: LTspice half bridge, double pulse at 75 V: lumped loop, 1.7 nH gate loop, 0.03 nH common source, 2 Ω on / 0 Ω off
Turn-on di/dt set by the driver (≈ 45 A/ns); turn-off di/dt grows with current
0.5 nH: 83 V at 79 A, !!101 V at 119 A!! per device
One device would carry 322 A peak ⇒ **current per device ≤ 80 A**

slides.title: Thermal path per device

paras: Two TIM layers and the cold plate dominate
Used for the decisions: **3.4 K/W**, coolant 60 °C
Bounds: 2.1 K/W (sintered stack), 8 K/W (gap pad)
R_{DS(on)}(T_{j}) from the datasheet: 1.49 at 100 °C, 1.80 at 150 °C

slides.title: n identical cells per switch (one device and one driver each)

paras: 228 A_{rms} per leg, 50 kHz, T_{j} and R_{DS(on)} solved together; LTspice energies at 0.5 nH

items.text: **4 EPC2361 per switch** (V_{DS} and T_{j} for all three R_{th}; 4 splits into two equal pairs)

slides.title: Where the loss comes from: line period and junction temperature

paras: n = 4, 50 kHz: switching loss follows |i| (plus a constant E_{oss} part), conduction loss follows i²
Conduction loss at the operating point is 28 % above its 25 °C value

slides.title: Losses vs number in parallel

items.text: Semiconductor losses only, 3.4 K/W, 60 °C coolant, 0.5 nH, 50 kHz; efficiency relative to 6.25 kW per leg.

slides.title: Switching frequency: losses, DC-link capacitors, current ripple

paras: (b) Voltage ripple sets the MLCC count below ≈ 99 kHz, ripple current above
(c) Winding current ripple Δi_{pp} = V_{m}/(4 L_{σ} f_{sw}) depends on the machine leakage inductance

items.text: f_{sw} ≥ 50 kHz (higher allowed by the machine); the DC link below is sized for 50 kHz

slides.title: Bypass capacitors: how many and how large

paras: **Bypass** (1 µF 0805) supplies the edge, **bank** (10 µF 1210) the f_{sw} ripple; per cell 81 A:
di/dt → number: L_{Cu} + ESL/n ≤ 0.5 nH ⇒ n ≥ 4
Edge charge ΔQ = I(t_{ri}/2 + t_{vf}) + Q_{oss} = 0.59 µC ⇒ 0.4 µF for 1.5 V
Hand-over to the bank through L_{b}: C_{bp} ≥ L_{b}(ΔI/ΔV)² = 2.9 µF (1 nH, 1.5 V): !!sets the value!!
Checks: C_{bp} ≫ C_{oss}; bypass–bank resonance ≈ 3 MHz ⇒ C_{bank} ≥ 10 C_{bp}

items.text: 6 × 1 µF 0805 per cell (2.7 µF eff.), unchanged on Rev B

slides.title: DC link of the Rev B leg and of one 75 V level

paras: Three-phase: no 2f power ripple, only f_{sw} ripple ⇒ hundreds of µF, not mF
Cap RMS current per level (Kolar, M = 1.15, cos φ = 0.9): ≈ 0.37 × 228 ≈ **85 A**, < 1 A per 1210 part
ΔV_{pp} ≈ Î/(8 f_{sw} C): one leg alone 3.2 V (4.3 %), !!three legs sharing ≈ 1.1 V (1.4 %)!! at 50 kHz
Bank ≥ 10 × bypass (240 µF): fulfilled

items.text: Keep all footprints; three legs share one bus per level (step 10); depopulate after the ripple measurement

slides.title: Can one driver drive all four?
slides.section: 7  Gate drive: from 4 devices to a building block

paras: One channel for 3 / 4 / 6 transistors: E_{on} per transistor +16 / +31 / +60 %
Peak sink current 12–14 A, above the 8 A rating
Longer gate tree brings the gate bump back
One driver per device: symmetric, but 4 channels and supplies per switch

slides.title: Why symmetry: current-sharing sensitivity

paras: Static sharing is fine (R_{DS(on)} has a positive TC)
Dynamic sharing is set by the gate circuits:
gate-loop mismatch 2 vs 8 nH → 19 % imbalance, 4:1 E_{on}
common source without Kelvin → 29 %, 2.8 × E_{on}
⇒ star gate network with Kelvin returns, one driver channel per pair

slides.title: Gate bump and negative off-voltage

paras: Bump ≈ Q_{GD}/C_{GS} ≈ 1.06 V, independent of current and voltage; close to the 0.8 V minimum threshold
With ≈ −1.2 V off-voltage the peak falls to ≈ 0 V; undershoot −2.3 V (rating −4 V); dead-time loss +0.1 W per leg

slides.title: Building block: two mirrored cells, one centre driver

paras: Two cells mirrored about the driver: identical gate loops and Kelvin returns
One 2EDF7275K channel drives a **pair** symmetrically (star network, R_{G} 0.5 Ω per transistor)
Each cell keeps its own commutation loop (0.374 nH per cell, Rev A Q3D)
Driver: 4 A / 8 A, separate turn-on (0.75 Ω) and turn-off (diode + 0 Ω) paths

items.text: Building block = 2 × EPC2361 per switch, one driver; **4 per switch = two blocks**

slides.title: Rev B: two blocks on one leg board
slides.section: 8  Four per switch on one board

items.text: Rev B leg board, 89.5 × 80 mm, 4 layers
4 × M4 → Cu bar → LEM HO 250-S → load

paras: Two Rev A blocks side by side: 4 cells, 2 drivers, star per pair unchanged
!!One DC link!! (87 MLCCs) and !!one switch node!!: AC of all four cells joined in a full-width 4-layer copper bus
Single output stub through one aperture Hall sensor: the controller sees one phase current
UFCS shunt in every LS source: same board for double-pulse and back-to-back load test
No short-circuit protection (lab board)

slides.title: Rev B leg board layout

paras: 89.5 × 80 mm, 4 layers, 236 parts
Cells at x = ±14.25 / ±33.25 mm, drivers at the block centres
Fischer LAM 4 heatsink rotated 90° (tube across the board) to clear the 27 mm shunts
DC terminals on the bottom edge, AC bus and terminals at the other edge
DRC 0 / 0 / 0; schematic generated from the PCB, netlist identical (0 problems)

slides.title: Two blocks on one switch node: driver skew

paras: Joining the AC in copper makes the inductance between the switch nodes of the two blocks (L_{x}) small
If block 2 switches Δt later, block 1 takes ΔI ≈ V_{m}·Δt / L_{x} until block 2 follows
Q3D (Rev B copper, step 11): L_{x} = 1.14 nH (HS on) / 1.08 nH (LS on) ⇒ **≈ 69 A per ns of skew**
Rev A deck required L_{x} ≳ 20 nH for two separate blocks; on one board the skew must be small instead

rows: same PCB, same CMC per block
U.FL V_{GS} of both blocks, UFCS per cell

items.text: Measure the per-cell current (UFCS) with both blocks switching; add delay trim in the C2000 if needed

slides.title: Gate supplies: two isolated supplies, Zener split

paras: One external isolated supply for all HS drivers and one for all LS drivers; each splits per driver through a WE-CNSW common-mode choke
5.1 V Zener VDD–S and 150 Ω bias resistor S–VEE (Karakaya, METU 2020, Fig. 4.1): V_{GS,on} = +5.1 V, V_{GS,off} = −(V_{ISO} − 5.1 V)
e.g. V_{ISO} = 6.3 V ⇒ −1.2 V off (bump mitigation); island decoupling 1 µF + 4.7 µF per rail

slides.title: Driver block: input filters, turn-on / turn-off paths, star

paras: Per block a 2×3 control header (12 V, GND, PWM_H, PWM_L, DIS) with common-mode chokes on each pair
47 Ω / 100 pF input filters, 10 k pull-downs, R_{ON} 0.75 Ω, R_{OFF} 0 Ω + Schottky, R_{G} 0.5 Ω per transistor

slides.title: Measurement and control

rows: Cu bar stub, JST to C2000

paras: Back-to-back load test, closed loop on a TI TMS320F28379D
UFCS continuous rating 50 A only up to +30 °C ambient: short load-test runs or forced air
No short-circuit protection on the board

slides.title: Power stage schematic (generated, identical to the PCB)
Three legs on one 75 V bus: what the bus must do

paras: The switching edge closes on each board (bypass + bank); the bus only carries the f_{sw} ripple between the leg banks
Sharing needs ωL_{bus} ≪ 1/(ωC): at 50 kHz and ≈ 250 µF eff. per leg L ≪ 40 nH ⇒ **target ≤ 5 nH leg to leg**
DC: 250 A stack current enters the level, 83 A per leg
All-MLCC banks joined by nH copper form a high-Q resonator ⇒ damping footprints

slides.title: PCB busbar: easy to manufacture

rows: 2 oz all layers (JLCPCB JLC3313); 3–4 oz option
L1 DC+ / ≤ 0.2 mm / L2 DC− / core / L3 DC+ / ≤ 0.2 mm / L4 DC−
12 × M4 onto the REDCUBE faces (6.5 mm)
2 × M6 lug pads at the centre leg (92 vias each)
frame holes with 8 mm Cu keep-out (1200 V)

paras: Estimate (μ_{0}·d·l/w): **0.28 nH** leg to leg
R per polarity and leg segment 0.27 mΩ (2 oz) ⇒ 7.5 W at 83 A per leg (3 oz: 5.0 W, 4 oz: 3.7 W)
Damping caps (100 V hybrid polymer) as DNP footprints; nylon standoffs at the leg corner holes
Generated: scripts/make_kicad_busbar.py, DRC clean

slides.title: Q3D: Rev B commutation loop per cell, with the shunt

paras: Rev A: **0.374 nH per cell** (same definition); Rev B mean: **0.84 nH per cell**
Increase = UFCS 120 pH + the LS source copper detour to the shunt pads; cells 1/3 (outer side of each block) are higher
Overshoot at 30 A/ns: v̂_{DS} ≈ 75 V + L·di/dt = !!100 V!! (target ≤ 90 V)
Routed Rev B copper: DCP, DCN, AC, LSRC1–4, ≈ 900 vias; 100 MHz; MLCC ESL 0.48 / 0.5 nH
Result from AC adaptive pass 2 (solve still converging)
Options: slower turn-on (R_{ON}, ≈ 20 A/ns ⇒ ≤ 90 V), shorten the LS source → shunt path, or accept the shunt for the DPT only (0 Ω link in the load test)

items.text: simulation/bb_q3d: revb_export.py, bb_q3d_revb.py, sd2matrix.py, revb_post.py (values in nH)

slides.title: Q3D: static current sharing and copper loss of the leg board

paras: Converged DC solve; FET 0.75 mΩ × 1.49 (100 °C), shunt 1 mΩ; DC terminals joined (bus), AC terminals joined (bar)
Board copper loss at 228 A_{rms}: !!40 W per leg!! (semiconductors ≈ 18 W); shunts ≈ 6.5 W
Static sharing is uneven: the inner cells (2, 4) carry ≈ 29 %, the outer cells (1, 3) ≈ 20–23 % ⇒ hotter inner cells
Cause: the copper path from each cell to the joined AC bus and to the DC terminals differs (cell position, AC columns on L3/L4)
Next layout iteration: widen the outer-cell AC columns / add AC copper on L1–L2, 2 oz → 3 oz, symmetric DC terminal placement

slides.title: Main PCB: findings from the Q3D extraction

rows: slower turn-on or shorter shunt path
layout iteration of the AC/DC copper

paras: The Rev B board works electrically (DRC clean, schematic = PCB) and is a good !!measurement!! board (UFCS per cell, U.FL)
Before a production-oriented layout: fix the sharing and loss (AC bus copper), and the driver skew (common PWM, delay trim, or a few nH between the blocks)
The double-pulse test on Rev B measures exactly these: per-cell current (UFCS), V_{DS} overshoot (U.FL), V_{GS} of both blocks

slides.title: Q3D: three legs on the PCB busbar

rows: Ripple of leg 1 at 50 kHz from legs 1 / 2 / 3
Busbar DC loss (250 A in, 3 × 83 A)

paras: Target ≤ 5 nH leg to leg met at 1 MHz; DC values are the low-frequency limit (current spread through all layers)
Network: Q3D matrices of three Rev B legs + busbar, MLCC banks with ESR/ESL and 35 % of C at 75 V; peaks in |Z| = inter-leg resonance
